Methods Text

Ready-to-paste text for the Methods section of your manuscript

Full paragraph
Quality control was performed using AnnQC v0.1.0 (Weisberg, 2026). Mitochondrial genes were identified by the 'mt-' prefix and ribosomal genes by the 'Rps|Rpl' prefix. Cells were filtered using manually specified thresholds: mitochondrial content ≤ 20%, minimum 500 genes per cell, minimum UMI count of 500. Gene-level filtering removed genes expressed in fewer than 3 cells. Doublet detection was not performed or was skipped. After quality control, following established best practices, 13,078 of 13,353 cells were retained (97.9%). Sensitivity analysis was performed using annqc sensitivity to assess the impact of threshold choices on cell retention and cluster composition, using independent threshold sweeps and combined strict/standard/permissive MAD-based profiles. AnnQC does not perform ambient RNA correction; tools such as CellBender or SoupX should be applied upstream if ambient RNA removal is required. All QC parameters and software versions are recorded in adata.uns['annqc'] for full reproducibility.
Short version (for abstracts)
scRNA-seq data were quality controlled using AnnQC v0.1.0 with standard thresholds, retaining 13,078 of 13,353 cells (97.9%) after removal of low-quality cells and doublets (ambient RNA correction not performed). Threshold sensitivity was assessed with annqc sensitivity.

Scrublet citation: Wolock SL, Lopez R, Klein AM. Scrublet: Computational Identification of Cell Doublets in Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data. Cell Syst. 2019;8(4):281–291.
